sections.html: Vieja (Cichlasoma) maculicauda, the Blackbelt Cichlid, is one of the larger Central American cichlids. Males can reach about 35 cm overall length.

The blackbelt cichlid, Vieja maculicauda, is a large cichlid found from the Usumacinta basin in Guatemala south to the River Chagres in Panama. It takes its name from the vertical black stripe around its flank and from its toughness. It lives in slow-moving rivers and lakes, sometimes in brackish or even marine conditions, and should only be kept with similarly aggressive fish of similar size.
Atlantic slope, from the Usumacinta River drainage in Guatemala to the Chagres River in Panama.

Found throughout much of Central America, where its range extends southwards from the River Usumacinta basin in Guatemala through Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica as far as the River Chagres in Panama.
In their distribution area they live in the lower sections of rivers where the current is slow and also go into brackish water.

Inhabits slow-moving and still parts of rivers as well as many lakes, especially over substrates of mud or sand. It is particularly associated with habitats centred around submerged branches and tree roots, or where aquatic and/or marginal vegetation grows densely. In certain parts of its range populations can be found living in brackish and occasionally even full marine conditions.
According to its size one needs voluminous aquaria, where their interesting social behaviour can be observed.

Standard length: 25.4 cm SL.

Aquarium base: 120 × 38 cm.

Volume: ~205 litres.

Example: 120 cm L x 45 cm H x 37.5 cm W - 213 litres.

Blackbelts like a sandy or fine gravel substrate. Simulate their natural habitat by providing lots of cover in the form of bits of wood (mopani, driftwood, bogwood). Blackbelt Cichlids thrive in lower lighting conditions so it may be beneficial to use floating plants to help dim the light.
Since they are able to tolerate brackish and marine conditions, they are unproblematic regarding water chemistry in aquaria.

• Temperature: 22–27°C
  • pH: 6.0 to 8.0, around 7.0 is optimal
  • Hardness: 8 to 16 dH

Fish of this size cannot be nourished with flake food alone. Beside granulated food and sticks they should be variedly fed. Here you can let your fantasy go and experiment a lot. Worms and insects as well as their larvae are greedily eaten, also vegetables should be offered, but here some individual differences exist in the readiness to eat these.

Almost exclusively herbivorous, although like most fish it still does best with a degree of protein in the diet. Wild fish graze on algae, detritus, fruits, nuts and both aquatic and terrestrial plant material.
This individuality is a part of the attraction with the care of large cichlids. Over years one becomes acquainted with them, so that sometimes they nearly belong to the family.
A fairly aggressive cichlid, should only be housed with similarly aggressive, similar sized fish. Will see smaller fish as food. Can be exceptionally aggressive when looking after fry.
Males are larger with more vivid colouration. Mature Blackbelt males will develop the nuchal hump on their head.

The Black belt Cichlid becomes sexually mature at around 15 centimetres in size, or at least 6 months old. Modify water parameters to be pretty much in the middle of the aforementioned water parameters - 26°C, pH 7 etc. 500 to 600 eggs will be laid on a flat piece of rock or stone. Eggs will be aggressively guarded and cleaned by the parents. Fry will hatch in 2 to 3 days and will be moved to previously created spawning pits all over the tank. A week later they will be free swimming.

The Blackbelt Cichlid gets its name from two things: firstly the vertical black stripe around its flank, and secondly its toughness. Vieja maculicauda is a tough, aggressive fish and should be respected as such. Maculicauda is a relatively easy fish to keep. They are not impossible to breed, but not the easiest fish either. If you seriously intend to breed this fish, it is a wise decision to house 6 juvenile fish in a large tank (212 litres at least), and let them pair off. When a pair has been found, rehome the other fish. A very interesting, colourful addition to a Central/North American aggressive cichlid tank.
